For a 50-person Indian company, I’d compare the commercial model rather than just headline ticket prices:

	MMT myBiz	ITILITE	FCM Travel
Platform/service fee	Negotiated service fee; 1.5% payment-gateway fee can apply	Pay-per-trip; no minimum monthly fee or platform fee	Custom TMC quote
Changes/cancellations	Supplier/airline rules apply; selected myBiz fares offer free changes/cancellation	No extra fee for support/modifications within same trip; supplier deductions still apply	Supplier charges can apply, potentially up to 100%; reissue fees may apply
Refunds	Depends on supplier fare; MMT facilitates refund	Booking cost refunded less airline/hotel deductions	Refund after FCM receives supplier funds
Support	24×7	24×7, human support	24×7 emergency assistance + dedicated consultant
Warranty/SLA	No blanket service warranty; contractual terms/order form govern	No travel “warranty”; transparent service model	No blanket warranty; negotiated programme/SLA
Best suited	Indian SME wanting broad inventory + GST/expense controls	50-person company wanting predictable transaction costs	Company wanting a genuinely managed TMC

MMT explicitly says it is an intermediary/aggregator, so the airline/hotel's cancellation terms remain critical. 
MakeMyTrip
+1

ITILITE is unusually transparent: its India pricing says there are no hidden costs, no minimum commitment, and changes/support don't add another fee. 
Itilite
+1

FCM is more traditional managed travel: dedicated consultants, account management, negotiated corporate inventory and 24/7 assistance, but pricing is quote-based. 
FCM Travel
+1

For procurement, get each vendor to quote the same 12-month scenario: 50 employees, expected monthly trips, domestic + international, and separately specify booking fee, cancellation/reissue fee, credit terms, GST, dedicated-agent SLA, after-hours SLA and implementation fee.
